questions.prompt: What is the first sign on Anthropic's list for using an LLM in customer support?

options.text: A small number of very complex, one-off questions.
options.explanation: The guide's first sign is the opposite: many similar questions.

options.text: A high volume of repetitive queries.
options.explanation: Right. The guide says this frees human agents for more complex issues.

options.text: A team that has no written answers to common questions.
options.explanation: That is not on the guide's list. Its first sign is a high volume of similar questions.

questions.prompt: A task saves 30 seconds each time and happens 40 times a month. Is it a strong first target?

options.text: Yes, because it repeats every single month.
options.explanation: Repetition alone isn't enough. 40 × 30 seconds is only 20 minutes a month.

options.text: No, the total time saved is very small.
options.explanation: Right. Multiply the time saved by the volume before you choose.

questions.prompt: Which kind of repeated work suits a batch job?

options.text: A live chat where a customer waits for each reply on screen.
options.explanation: A customer is waiting. Batch jobs are for work that doesn't need an immediate response.

options.text: A phone call that needs an answer within a few seconds.
options.explanation: Batch results can take up to 24 hours on OpenAI's page, so this is a poor fit.

options.text: Summarizing 5,000 contracts that are needed next week.
options.explanation: Right. Both vendors' batch pages describe large volumes that don't need an immediate response, at 50% lower cost.
